reviews.review: A good third person melee/shooter ala Gear of War. The story isn't all that great and there are some difficulty spikes but the action is fun throughout.

Seems pretty fun, only two gripes with it so far.

Random almost crashes where the screen goes black for a second, but the game resumes a second later. I assume it's just a windows 10 bug.

And rocket dude orcs. Not the big ones, the small ones. They do about 100k damage per shot, activly punish you for going into melee and spawn in EVERY BATTLE after the first 5-6 levels.

Sure I wanted a challenge, but I didn't want to have to resort to darksouls levels of ♥♥♥♥♥-fighting just because I cannot effectivly melee them all before getting rocketed into last year. Yeah I CAN pass a level first try by sitting at the back and sniping them all, but the whole point of having an execution system and making it your only way to regain hp is to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ beat the ♥♥♥♥ out of some greenskins.
Unfortunatly, the execution animation takes so long for each enemy, that one rocket orc can do aproximatly 110% of your health in about half of the animation.

So here I am, stuck on some mission about 3 hours into the game because the next fight has heaps of bazerkers and nobs for me to fight, but rocket dudes sitting on every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ wall, roof, crevice and generally mixed through the fight. Even getting anywhere near them without dying is a challenge, so I will probably have to just sit in the back and shoot them all with my guns, instead of having fun.

Great.

It's either that or lower the difficulty (if you even can change during the missions) but this game has such random difficulty spikes (is there a rocket boy within 2 miles? if no, fight is challenging but doable, if yes, ingest pill located below seat) that I don't really feel like making the game super easy.

Other than wishing I could summon a bunch of flesh flayers into the nearest orc rocket scientist's rear every once in a while, I'm having fun.
Excuse any spelling, it's currently nope'o'clock and this doesn't have a spellcheck.

Warhammer 40k: Spacemarine is a game so caught up in doing a half-arsed job of emulating other successful games, it has no identity of its own. The gunplay is a poor knock-off of Gears of War and the melee combat is a poor knock-off of Arkham Asylum, and the difficulty alternates between snooze fest to rage fest between each encounter. 

Melee combat has only half a dozen moves per weapon (with just three weapons) and performing the same ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ finishing move over and over again to regenerate health is a wearying necessity to stay alive, so wading out into the fray is more of a chore than the visceral joy it should be. 

This is especially true when the ork rocket troopers are introduced en masse as, with no a cover system and a character who moves with all the speed and grace of a sack of potatoes, you'll be obliterated in seconds flat if you aren't constantly leaching enemies for health.

The story is uninspired, too. No spoilers here but if you're familiar with the 40k universe, it's pretty predictable stuff.

If I had to say something positive about this game, it would be about how appealing the art style and lore is. Then again, considering that these was borrowed from Games Workshop and aren't added to in any meaningful way, it's not credit which the developers are due. The guns feel ok, I suppose, nothing to get too excited about though. Seriously, if I weren't such a fan of Warhammer, there's no way I would have soldiered on to the five hour mark before quitting for good.

There is no reason to play Space Marine. Play one of the Gears of War games or Arkham games or, if you want to play something set in the 40k universe, one of the Dawn of War games. Relic should stick to strategy games, they're out of their element here.
I wish my recommendation makes somebody someday buy this game, I enjoy it a lot because the system so far is well balanced buuuuuut with a little population of players though...
Even though it's short, the story is pretty cool and it's packed with action.
